zh.title: 17歲嫌犯衝入樸茲茅斯機場撞毀PC-12
zh.summary: 17歲駕駛衝入機場撞毀PlaneSense PC-12；嫌犯被捕將出庭
body: 8月29日晚間約20時09分，一名17歲駕駛為逃避新罕布夏州警攔截，闖入樸茲茅斯國際機場（PSM）圍籬，撞上庫伯塔拖車後再撞擊停泊的PlaneSense Pilatus PC-12。
PlaneSense證實該PC-12當時在總部待維修，機身左翼斷裂、起落架塌陷，損毀嚴重，但無員工受傷，飛行業務未受影響。
警方已逮捕駕駛Wyatt Seely，依加重酒駕、魯莽駕駛、抗拒警員及肇逃等輕罪起訴，定於9月9日在樸茲茅斯地方法院出庭。

en.title: Teen fleeing police crashes into PlaneSense PC-12 at Portsmouth Airport
en.summary: Teen crashes stolen Mustang into parked PlaneSense PC-12 at Portsmouth Airport; driver charged
body: Around 20:09 local time on 29 August 2026, a 17‑year‑old driver fleeing New Hampshire State Police crashed through the perimeter fence of Portsmouth International Airport (PSM), striking a Kubota ground‑support tractor and then a parked PlaneSense Pilatus PC‑12.

PlaneSense confirmed the PC‑12 was at its headquarters awaiting routine maintenance; the aircraft suffered a severed left wing and collapsed landing gear, but no employees were injured and flight operations continued unaffected.

The driver, identified as Wyatt Seely of Rochester, was taken into custody and charged with aggravated DWI, reckless driving, disobeying an officer and conduct after an accident; he is scheduled to appear in Portsmouth District Court on 9 September.

He is scheduled to appear in Portsmouth District Court on September 9.

zh.title: Vueling推遲B737 MAX服役 座椅認證延誤
zh.summary: Vueling確認B737 MAX延至2027上半年服役；RECARO座椅認證拖延
body: 巴塞隆納廉價航空Vueling確認推遲引進波音737 MAX機隊，新服役目標推至2027年上半年。根據西班牙媒體報導，此次延期乃因RECARO座椅認證流程漫長，Vueling已證實正與RECARO協商解決，預計延誤將持續數月。
國際航空集團（IAG）於2019年巴黎航展下單150架B737 MAX（含50架確定訂單與100架選擇權），Vueling初期獲分配50架。2026年5月，IAG行使10架選擇權，Vueling配置增至60架。
ch-aviation數據顯示，截至2026年9月2日，Vueling機隊共137架，其中97架為A320ceo，另有A320neo、A321neo、A321ceo與A319。該航司計劃在數年內完成向全波音機隊的轉型。
首批引進機型為737 MAX 8-200，配置197座艙位，較現行A320的189座多出8席。737 MAX 10（IAG至少訂購25架）將於型別認證後陸續加入，認證預計2026年第四季完成。
原定首航安排為2026年12月巴塞隆納（BCN）飛阿利坎特（ALC），隨後開闢塞維亞（SVQ）、馬略卡島（PMI）與羅馬（FCO）航線，現須配合新時程調整。
座椅認證延誤已波及多家歐洲航空：漢莎航空被迫以無新款Allegris頭等艙座椅執飛部分航班，荷蘭皇家航空預計新引進A350將缺乏商務艙配置。

en.title: Vueling Postpones Boeing 737 MAX Entry Into Service to First Half 2027 Over Seat Certification Delays
en.summary: Vueling delays 737 MAX launch to H1 2027; RECARO seat certification issues cited
body: Barcelona-based low-cost carrier Vueling has confirmed it will postpone the entry into service of its new Boeing 737 MAX fleet, pushing the target date to the first half of 2027. According to Spanish media reports, the delay stems from the protracted certification process for RECARO seats slated for installation. Vueling has acknowledged it is in discussions with RECARO to resolve the issue, though the setback is expected to last several months.

The aircraft originate from International Airlines Group (IAG)'s 2019 Paris Air Show order for 150 737 MAX jets (50 firm orders plus 100 options). Vueling was initially allocated 50 aircraft; in May 2026 IAG exercised 10 options, raising Vueling's allocation to 60.

Per ch-aviation data dated 2 September 2026, Vueling operates 137 aircraft, predominantly 97 Airbus A320ceos alongside A320neos, A321neos, A321ceos and A319s. The airline intends to transition to an all-Boeing fleet over several years.

The first batch will be the 737 MAX 8-200 configured with 197 seats — eight more than the current 189-seat A320 layout. The 737 MAX 10 (IAG has at least 25 on order) will join later, contingent on type certification expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Vueling's inaugural commercial 737 MAX flight was scheduled for December 2026 on the Barcelona (BCN) to Alicante (ALC) route, followed by services to Sevilla (SVQ), Palma de Mallorca (PMI) and Rome Fiumicino (FCO). That schedule must now be revised.

Seat certification delays have recently affected other European carriers: Lufthansa has flown some aircraft without its new Allegris First Class seats, and KLM is expected to debut its Airbus A350s without a business class cabin.

facts.claim: Vueling postpones Boeing 737 MAX entry into service to first half of 2027

facts.claim: Delay caused by protracted RECARO seat certification process
facts.sourceQuote: According to Spanish media reports, the postponement, which adds to other prior delays, is due to the protracted certification process of the RECARO seats which are expected to be fitted onboard.

facts.claim: Vueling confirmed discussions with RECARO to resolve seat certification issue
facts.sourceQuote: Vueling has confirmed it is in conversation with RECARO to solve the issue, although the delay is expected to take several months.

facts.claim: IAG 2019 order for 150 737 MAX; Vueling allocation raised to 60 in May 2026
facts.sourceQuote: Vueling was initially allocated 50 aircraft from the mega-order IAG placed at the 2019 Paris Air Show for 150 B737 MAX aircraft (which included 50 firm orders and 100 options). In May 2026, this figure was increased to 60 aircraft after IAG exercised 10 of those options.

facts.claim: Vueling fleet 137 aircraft as of 2 September 2026, mostly A320ceos; plans all-Boeing transition
facts.sourceQuote: According to ch-aviation data, as of September 2, 2026, Vueling has a fleet of 137 aircraft, the majority of which (97 aircraft) are A320ceos, but also includes several A320neo, A321 (both neo and ceo) and A319 aircraft.

zh.title: 阿聯酋航空獲Skytrax高端經濟艙獎 但腿部空間不如日本航空
zh.summary: 阿聯酋航空奪Skytrax高端經濟艙獎；腿部空間較日本航空少
body: 根據 Simple Flying 報導，阿聯酋航空在最新 Skytrax 獎項中奪得高端經濟艙座椅類別冠軍，成為全球最舒適高端經濟艙的得主。
同報導指出，阿聯酋航空該艙等腿部空間仍少於日本航空同級產品，顯示舒適度不完全取決於腿部空間大小。
Simple Flying 強調此獎項僅涉及座椅設計評分，並未將腿部空間納為唯一判斷標準。
讀者可參考該報導以了解完整評比細節與數據比較。
報導發布於 2026 年 9 月 2 日。

en.title: Emirates wins Skytrax premium economy award despite less legroom than Japan Airlines
en.summary: Emirates wins Skytrax premium economy award; legroom less than Japan Airlines
body: According to Simple Flying, Emirates captured the Skytrax premium economy seat category, being named the world’s most comfortable premium economy product.
The same report notes that Emirates’ premium economy still offers less legroom than the comparable Japan Airlines product, indicating comfort is not solely determined by legroom.
Simple Flying emphasises that the award reflects seat design scores and does not make legroom the sole criterion; the article was published on 2 September 2026.
Readers can consult the full Simple Flying piece for detailed scoring methodology and comparative data. The publication date is 2 September 2026.
